issue.title: Same-plan %wait on a proc unit resolves at supervisor submission, not terminal proc status
issue.description:
Two spellings of "wait for this proc" have different completion semantics in the typed launch path.

A same-plan logical wait on a proc unit resolves as soon as that unit has any launch outcome: `resolved_wait_outcome` in `sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/admission.rs` (~line 523) returns an outcome for a `WaitTargetWire::Logical` target when `state.phase.outcome()` is `Some`, and `Launched` (set when the proc's supervisor submission succeeds) satisfies it. So `%wait` on a same-plan proc means "proc submitted", not "proc finished".

An external proc wait (`%wait(proc=<id|shell>)`) instead polls the proc record until a terminal proc status via `_resolve_proc_wait` in `src/sase/agent/launch_admission_runtime.py`.

The dependent unit in the same plan can therefore start while the proc it "waited for" is still running, which contradicts both the external-wait semantics and the natural reading of the directive.

Remediation direction (from the reverse-wait-hold-barrier research consolidation): either make same-plan proc waits resolve at terminal proc settlement, or add an explicit satisfaction mode (`Launched` vs `Terminal`) to the wait wire so the two behaviors are distinct and deliberate. Any new reverse-wait/hold feature must key off terminal settlement only and must not inherit this ambiguity.

Found while consolidating research for the proposed `%sink`/`%hold` reverse-wait directive (research repo: `202609/reverse_wait_hold_barrier/reverse_wait_hold_barrier.md`, section 3.6).

task_type_fields.impact: Same-plan sequencing after a proc silently races the proc instead of following it; any feature built on logical waits (e.g. the proposed %hold reverse-wait barrier) would inherit wrong completion semantics if it reused these edges.
task_type_fields.repro: Submit one typed launch plan with a %proc unit plus an agent unit that %waits on it (logical wait). Observe the agent unit becomes eligible as soon as the proc reaches the Launched admission phase (supervisor submission), while the proc is still running; an external %wait(proc=<id>) on the same proc from another launch blocks until terminal status.
